nodes.title: Connecting ComfyUI to ZMongo Database
widgets_values:
## 🚀 How to Log In and Connect ComfyUI to ZMongo

Connecting your local ComfyUI workflow to the backend database architecture requires only a single configuration node. Follow this step-by-step guide to authenticate your session using either the standard workflow properties or the integrated ZMongo panel layout.

---

### Step 1: Add the API Key Session Node

1. Open your ComfyUI workspace interface.


2. **Right-click** anywhere on the empty workspace grid canvas.


3. Search for or navigate to **`00 API Key Session`** (`ZMongoApiKeySessionNode`) and click it to add the configuration block to your workflow.



---

### Step 2: Configure Your Credentials Using the Panel

Inside the **`00 API Key Session`** node, update the text fields with your personal credentials:

* **`base_url`**: Set this to your backend server address: `https://businessprocessapplications.com`.


* **`zai_api_key`**: Register an account on the platform, navigate to the **User Settings** tab to retrieve your unique token, and paste your private alphanumeric API key here.
* **`username`**: Type in your assigned account username (for example, `comfyguest`).



> 💡 **Tip:** Leave all other routing paths (like `/comfy-zmongo` or `/fleet`), `timeout_seconds` (30), and verification switches (`verify_tls`, `test_whoami`) at their default settings unless explicitly instructed otherwise by an administrator.
> 
> 

---

### Step 3: Verify Your Connection via UI Preview Panels

To confirm that your session has successfully logged in and is routing to the correct user silo space without dropping background database connection errors:

1. Connect a **`PreviewAny`** or text display node to the output slots of your **`00 API Key Session`** configuration node.


2. Click **Queue Prompt** on your ComfyUI panel.



When your connection successfully routes to the unified backend, the **Preview as Text** panels will automatically update with an authenticated success status showing your active database properties:

#### Output Slot 1: Active Configuration Profile

```json
{
  "data": {
    "auth_db_name": "auth",
    "db_name": "comfyguest",
    "r2_active": true,
    "repo_class": "GuardedZMongo",
    "silo_db_name": "comfyguest",
    "username": "comfyguest"
  },
  "error": null,
  "message": "Authenticated.",
  "status_code": 200,
  "success": true
}

```

#### Output Slot 2: Authentication Quick Status

```text
Authenticated.

```

Once this status returns `Authenticated.`, your active database session flows natively to all downstream database components. Any documents or assets created using the ComfyUI API nodes will immediately appear inside your browser-based Manager UI dashboard. You can now securely read, write, and manage your collections directly within your pipeline workspace!
